      "title": "Team admin/owner authorization check uses AND instead of OR",
      "body": "In addGuestsHandler, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. The name and permission intent are admin OR owner, but the code requires the user to satisfy both checks. Depending on how the role queries treat OWNER/ADMIN, legitimate team admins (and possibly owners) will be denied access to add guests. Replace `&&` with `||`."
    },

      "severity": "high",

      "title": "Calendar update uses requester's credentials instead of booking owner's credentials",
      "body": "addGuestsHandler constructs EventManager with `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, even though the mutation is allowed for attendees and team admins/owners. External calendar events are normally owned by the booking organizer/host, so using the requester's credentials can fail to update the correct calendar or update nothing. The handler loads `booking.user.credentials` but does not use them. Use the booking owner/host (or the credentials associated with the destination calendar) for the calendar update."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",
      "line": 44,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "No booking status check before adding guests",
      "body": "After loading the booking, addGuestsHandler only checks existence and permissions. It does not reject cancelled, rejected, or otherwise inactive bookings. The API can therefore add attendees to cancelled or past bookings, send notification emails, and attempt calendar updates for events that should no longer be modified. Add a status/eligibility check (for example, only upcoming accepted bookings unless intentionally broader)."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",
      "line": 74,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Guest emails are not normalized or deduplicated server-side",
      "body": "In addGuestsHandler, `uniqueGuests` filters input emails case-sensitively and does not remove duplicates within the request. As a result, `guests: [\"a@example.com\", \"A@Example.com\"]` or repeated emails can create duplicate attendee rows or bypass the existing-attendee check. The blacklist comparison is also case-sensitive because only the blacklist is lowercased, so `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` can be bypassed with uppercase input. Normalize (trim/lowercase) and deduplicate guest emails before comparing, persisting, and sending emails."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",
      "line": 168,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Email dispatch receives original guests instead of actually added guests",
      "body": "addGuestsHandler calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` after filtering to `uniqueGuests`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses the supplied list to decide whether an attendee receives the new-guest invitation or the existing-attendee notification. If the original `guests` array contains duplicates, blacklisted emails, existing attendee emails, or case variants, the wrong email template can be sent (for example, an existing attendee may be treated as a new guest). Pass the normalized `uniqueGuests` list that was actually inserted."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",
      "line": 60,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Bookings without a user crash when looking up organizer",
      "body": "addGuestsHandler does `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. For bookings where `userId` is null (possible for some team bookings), this queries user id 0 and throws, producing an error instead of handling the team/organizer case. The handler should support bookings without a direct user or fall back to the appropriate team/primary email."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/emails/email-manager.ts",
      "line": 525,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Add-guests emails ignore event-type email disable settings",
      "body": "`sendAddGuestsEmails` sends organizer/host and attendee emails unconditionally. Other email flows accept `eventTypeMetadata` and check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`/`eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, respecting `disableStandardEmails` settings. This new flow does not, so emails can be sent even when the event type is configured to suppress host or attendee standard emails. Pass and honor event-type metadata."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts",
      "line": 5,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Guests array is unbounded",
      "body": "The mutation schema allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no maximum length or minimum count. A client can submit an arbitrarily large number of emails, causing bulk attendee creation and mass email fan-out. Add a reasonable `.min(1).max(N)` and server-side uniqueness validation."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx",
      "line": 43,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Error toast fallback is unreachable",
      "body": "In AddGuestsDialog, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a non-empty string, so `showToast(message || t(\"unable_to_add_guests\"), ...)` never uses the fallback. If `err.data?.code` or `err.message` is missing, users may see `undefined: ...` instead of a friendly message. Build the message conditionally."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx",
      "line": 61,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Dialog state is not consistently reset when closed",
      "body": "AddGuestsDialog resets `multiEmailValue` only on cancel or successful mutation, and does not reset `isInvalidEmail` on success. Closing via `onOpenChange` (for example, Escape or overlay click) leaves previous emails and validation errors in state, so reopening can show stale values or stale invalid-email warnings. Reset form state whenever the dialog closes or opens."

Maintainers would want coverage for organizer/attendee/team admin permissions, cancelled bookings, duplicate/case-variant emails, blacklisted emails, and the email template selection."

findings.title: Team admin/owner authorization check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: In addGuestsHandler, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. The name and permission intent are admin OR owner, but the code requires the user to satisfy both checks. Depending on how the role queries treat OWNER/ADMIN, legitimate team admins (and possibly owners) will be denied access to add guests. Replace `&&` with `||`.

findings.title: Calendar update uses requester's credentials instead of booking owner's credentials
findings.body: addGuestsHandler constructs EventManager with `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, even though the mutation is allowed for attendees and team admins/owners. External calendar events are normally owned by the booking organizer/host, so using the requester's credentials can fail to update the correct calendar or update nothing. The handler loads `booking.user.credentials` but does not use them. Use the booking owner/host (or the credentials associated with the destination calendar) for the calendar update.

findings.title: No booking status check before adding guests
findings.body: After loading the booking, addGuestsHandler only checks existence and permissions. It does not reject cancelled, rejected, or otherwise inactive bookings. The API can therefore add attendees to cancelled or past bookings, send notification emails, and attempt calendar updates for events that should no longer be modified. Add a status/eligibility check (for example, only upcoming accepted bookings unless intentionally broader).

findings.title: Guest emails are not normalized or deduplicated server-side
findings.body: In addGuestsHandler, `uniqueGuests` filters input emails case-sensitively and does not remove duplicates within the request. As a result, `guests: ["a@example.com", "A@Example.com"]` or repeated emails can create duplicate attendee rows or bypass the existing-attendee check. The blacklist comparison is also case-sensitive because only the blacklist is lowercased, so `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` can be bypassed with uppercase input. Normalize (trim/lowercase) and deduplicate guest emails before comparing, persisting, and sending emails.

findings.title: Email dispatch receives original guests instead of actually added guests
findings.body: addGuestsHandler calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` after filtering to `uniqueGuests`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses the supplied list to decide whether an attendee receives the new-guest invitation or the existing-attendee notification. If the original `guests` array contains duplicates, blacklisted emails, existing attendee emails, or case variants, the wrong email template can be sent (for example, an existing attendee may be treated as a new guest). Pass the normalized `uniqueGuests` list that was actually inserted.

findings.title: Bookings without a user crash when looking up organizer
findings.body: addGuestsHandler does `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. For bookings where `userId` is null (possible for some team bookings), this queries user id 0 and throws, producing an error instead of handling the team/organizer case. The handler should support bookings without a direct user or fall back to the appropriate team/primary email.

findings.title: Add-guests emails ignore event-type email disable settings
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends organizer/host and attendee emails unconditionally. Other email flows accept `eventTypeMetadata` and check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`/`eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, respecting `disableStandardEmails` settings. This new flow does not, so emails can be sent even when the event type is configured to suppress host or attendee standard emails. Pass and honor event-type metadata.

findings.title: Guests array is unbounded
findings.body: The mutation schema allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no maximum length or minimum count. A client can submit an arbitrarily large number of emails, causing bulk attendee creation and mass email fan-out. Add a reasonable `.min(1).max(N)` and server-side uniqueness validation.

findings.title: Error toast fallback is unreachable
findings.body: In AddGuestsDialog, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a non-empty string, so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)` never uses the fallback. If `err.data?.code` or `err.message` is missing, users may see `undefined: ...` instead of a friendly message. Build the message conditionally.

findings.title: Dialog state is not consistently reset when closed
findings.body: AddGuestsDialog resets `multiEmailValue` only on cancel or successful mutation, and does not reset `isInvalidEmail` on success. Closing via `onOpenChange` (for example, Escape or overlay click) leaves previous emails and validation errors in state, so reopening can show stale values or stale invalid-email warnings. Reset form state whenever the dialog closes or opens.

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip in MultiEmail
findings.body: The remove-email control uses `<Tooltip content="Remove email">`, which is not localized through `t()`. Users in non-English locales will see English text. Use a translation key.

findings.title: No tests for new addGuests mutation
findings.body: The PR introduces a privileged mutation with nontrivial permission checks, guest deduplication/case handling, blacklist filtering, calendar updates, and email selection, but no automated tests are included. Maintainers would want coverage for organizer/attendee/team admin permissions, cancelled bookings, duplicate/case-variant emails, blacklisted emails, and the email template selection.
